# Moonshot AI Kimi K2.6 now available on Workers AI

@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 is now available on Workers AI, in partnership with Moonshot AI for Day 0 support. Kimi K2.6 is a native multimodal agentic model from Moonshot AI that advances practical capabilities in long-horizon coding, coding-driven design, proactive autonomous execution, and swarm-based task orchestration.

Built on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 1T total parameters and 32B active per token, Kimi K2.6 delivers frontier-scale intelligence with efficient inference. It scores competitively against GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6 on agentic and coding benchmarks, including BrowseComp (83.2), SWE-Bench Verified (80.2), and Terminal-Bench 2.0 (66.7).

## Key capabilities

- 262.1k token context window for retaining full conversation history, tool definitions, and codebases across long-running agent sessions
- Long-horizon coding with significant improvements on complex, end-to-end coding tasks across languages including Rust, Go, and Python
- Coding-driven design that transforms simple prompts and visual inputs into production-ready interfaces and full-stack workflows
- Agent swarm orchestration scaling horizontally to 300 sub-agents executing 4,000 coordinated steps for complex autonomous tasks
- Vision inputs for processing images alongside text
- Thinking mode with configurable reasoning depth
- Multi-turn tool calling for building agents that invoke tools across multiple conversation turns

## Differences from Kimi K2.5

If you are migrating from Kimi K2.5, note the following API changes:

- K2.6 useschat_template_kwargs.thinking to control reasoning, replacing chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking
- K2.6 returns reasoning content in thereasoning field, replacing reasoning_content

## Get started

Use Kimi K2.6 through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()), the REST API at /ai/run, or the OpenAI-compatible endpoint at /v1/chat/completions. You can also use AI Gateway with any of these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Kimi K2.6 model page and pricing.

# Moonshot AI Kimi K2.7 Code now available on Workers AI

@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code is now available on Workers AI. Kimi K2.7 Code is a code-optimized variant of the Kimi K2 family, built on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with 1T total parameters and 32B active per token.

## Improved coding and agent performance

K2.7 Code delivers meaningful gains over K2.6 on coding and agentic benchmarks:

- +21.8% on Kimi Code Bench v2
- +11.0% on Program Bench
- +31.5% on MLS Bench Lite

## Reasoning efficiency

K2.7 Code uses 30% fewer reasoning tokens compared to K2.6, reducing overthinking and lowering inference cost for reasoning-heavy workloads.

## Key capabilities

- 262.1k token context window for retaining full conversation history, tool definitions, and codebases across long-running agent sessions
- Long-horizon coding with improved instruction following and higher end-to-end coding task success rates
- Vision inputs for processing images alongside text
- Thinking mode with configurable reasoning depth viachat_template_kwargs.thinking
- Multi-turn tool calling for building agents that invoke tools across multiple conversation turns
- Structured outputs with JSON schema support

## Differences from Kimi K2.6

If you are migrating from Kimi K2.6, note the following:

- K2.7 Code is optimized for coding tasks with improved benchmark performance and reasoning efficiency
- Cached input token pricing is $0.19 per M tokens (vs $0.16 for K2.6)
- API usage is identical — no parameter changes required

## Get started

Use Kimi K2.7 Code through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()), the REST API at /ai/run, or the OpenAI-compatible endpoint at /v1/chat/completions. You can also use AI Gateway with any of these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Kimi K2.7 Code model page and pricing.

Kimi.content:
Kimi K3.1 Pro 開放權重模型推升中國 AI 下載量至 1000 億次

關鍵要點

Moonshot AI 於 2026 年 11 月 21 日發布 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的完整模型權重，使其成為全球參數規模最大的開源模型。

根據 OpenRouter 平台數據，中國模型在 11 月 9 日至 15 日期間的每週 token 用量達 1.191 兆個，連續 29 週位居全球第一。

Kimi K3 引入混合式線性注意力機制，能以更低成本處理超長文本，並提升超大型模型訓練的穩定性。

北京月之暗面 AI（月之暗面科技股份有限公司）於 2026 年 11 月 21 日發布 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的完整模型權重。據《人民日報》報導，這是全球參數規模最大的開源模型。此次發布在科技界引發廣泛討論，也標誌著中國開源 AI 生態系統的一個里程碑；中國本土模型的全球累計下載量已超過 100 億次。

開源模型運動反映了 AI 能力在全球分配方式的根本轉變。不同於傳統軟體發布原始碼，開源模型會開放「權重」供下載及本機部署——這些權重是數以兆計的參數值，編碼了模型學習到的語言模式、推理能力和知識。這種方式讓企業和開發者能在自己的電腦或伺服器上執行推論，針對特定任務微調模型，並部署於私有基礎架構，而無須投入大量資金從頭訓練模型。

中國開源模型已在全球聚合平台上建立明確的市場領先地位。在 11 月 9 日至 15 日當週，OpenRouter 全球開源模型聚合平台上的中國模型每週呼叫量達 1.191 兆個代幣，連續 29 週位居全球第一。這波增長反映了技術進步，以及中國 AI 生態系統內廣泛的商業採用。

代幣呼叫量已成為衡量 AI 活動和產業滲透深度的重要指標。中國每日代幣呼叫量已超過 500萬兆，電商平台如今也設有代幣充值中心，而代幣在「雙十一」購物節期間成為高需求項目。中央網信辦副主任王京濤指出，代幣具備可衡量、可定價、可交易的屬性，正逐步被運用為觀察 AI 活力、產業滲透深度及智慧化發展水準的重要指標。

架構創新與技術突破提升競爭力

中國開源模型競爭力的提升，不僅源自廣泛的應用範圍，也得益於快速的架構創新與基礎技術突破。由 Deep Seek 開發的 DeepSeek 自去年年初起陸續發布 DeepSeek 系列模型，透過混合專家模型架構創新取得效能突破，大幅降低推論成本和運算需求。此架構隨後成為全球 AI 領域共同探索的方向。

Moonshot AI 今年發布的 Kimi K3 引入自行開發的混合線性注意力機制，讓「超長文本運算成本更低，超大型模型訓練更穩定」。Moonshot AI Kimi 部門創辦人暨執行長楊植麟表示：「我們從基礎邏輯出發，重新建構這套架構的關鍵組件，讓模型訓練得以探索新的演化空間。中國開源模型正成為全球模型製造商評測的基準，以及海外研究機構的重要研究樣本。」

中國開源模型與國產算力的相容性也顯著提升。2026 年 6 月，美團發布了一款完全使用國產算力訓練和推論的兆參數大型語言模型。11 月，美團新一代大型模型 LongCat—2.5 發布，推動基於國產算力的大模型從「能跑」邁向「跑得快、跑得省」。美團 LongCat 大模型負責人蔡勛亮表示：「我們逐步克服了神經網路處理器確定性運算、提升算力利用率等挑戰，驗證了大規模國產模型訓練的可行性。」

國內晶片製造商也持續最佳化產品設計，以推動 AI 部署。國內推論 GPU 製造商曦望董事長徐冰表示：「中國開源模型能力的提升，正推動智慧體、程式設計和影片生成需求加速增長，這將帶來大量需要處理長上下文及高效能多模態並行處理的高頻呼叫。隨著呼叫規模增加，使用者對回應速度和使用成本會更加敏感。」

深度產業整合與全球普及

中國開源模型正深入各種應用場景。在 BOE 通宵運作的生產線上，人工智慧系統即時捕捉顯示面板的微小缺陷，立即生成修復方案並協調設備完成修復，形成從問題檢測、分析到執行的端到端智慧品質管理閉環。

個人開發者吳睿萌接到一位淘寶店主的需求，想將動漫風格圖像應用於車膜；他立即察覺到「AI 試穿」場景的商機。他使用無程式碼應用開發平台「秒搭」，只花 25 分鐘便設計出展示版，最終以 8000 元售出這個「+AI」概念。吳表示：「只要用自然語言描述需求，模型就能打造客製化應用，人工智慧也能幫我補足能力上的不足。」

# xAI Grok OAuth (SuperGrok / X Premium+)

Hermes Agent supports xAI Grok through a browser-based OAuth device-code login flow against accounts.x.ai, using either a SuperGrok subscription (grok.com) or an X Premium+ subscription (linked X account). NoXAI_API_KEY is required — log in once and Hermes automatically refreshes your session in the background. Comparing the two products? Hermes Agent vs Grok Bot covers model choice, platforms and pricing with sources.

When you sign in with an X account that has Premium+, xAI automatically links the subscription status to your xAI session, so the OAuth flow works the same as it does for direct SuperGrok subscribers.

The transport reuses thecodex_responses adapter (xAI exposes a Responses-style endpoint), so reasoning, tool-calling, streaming, and prompt caching work without any adapter changes.

The same OAuth bearer token is also reused by every direct-to-xAI surface in Hermes — TTS, image generation, video generation, and transcription — so a single login covers all four.

## Overview

Item | Value 
---|---
Provider ID | xai-oauth 
Display name | xAI Grok OAuth (SuperGrok / X Premium+) 
Auth type | Browser OAuth 2.0 device code 
Transport | xAI Responses API (codex_responses) 
Default model | grok-4.6 
Endpoint | https://api.x.ai/v1 
Auth server | https://accounts.x.ai 
Requires env var | No (XAI_API_KEY is not used for this provider) 
Subscription | SuperGrok or X Premium+ — see note below 

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.9+
- Hermes Agent installed
- An active SuperGrok subscription on your xAI account, or an X Premium+ subscription on the X account you sign in with (xAI links the subscription automatically)
- A browser available anywhere you can open the printed verification URL

xAI may restrict OAuth API access by tier

xAI's backend enforces its own allowlist on the OAuth API surface and has been seen to reject standard SuperGrok subscribers withHTTP 403 (see issue #26847) even though the in-app subscription is active. If OAuth login succeeds in the browser but inference returns 403, set XAI_API_KEY and switch to the API-key path (provider: xai) — that surface is not subject to the same gating today.

## Quick Start
# Launch the provider and model picker
hermes model
# → Select "xAI Grok OAuth (SuperGrok / X Premium+)" from the provider list
# → Hermes opens or prints an accounts.x.ai verification URL
# → Enter the displayed code if prompted, then approve access in the browser
# → Pick a model (grok-4.6 is at the top)
# → Start chatting

hermes

After the first login, credentials are stored under~/.hermes/auth.json and refreshed automatically before they expire.

## Logging In Manually

You can trigger a login without going through the model picker:
hermes auth add xai-oauth

### Remote / headless sessions

On servers, containers, browser-only consoles (Cloud Shell, Codespaces, EC2 Instance Connect), or SSH sessions where Hermes cannot open a browser locally, Hermes prints the xAI verification URL and user code. Open the URL in any browser on your laptop or in the cloud console, enter the code if prompted, and Hermes will keep polling until xAI approves the login. No SSH tunnel or local callback listener is required.
hermes auth add xai-oauth --no-browser
# Open the printed verification URL in your browser.

The same device-code flow applies when you sign in from the web dashboard or the desktop app: Hermes shows the verification URL and user code, then polls in the background until you approve access.

## How the Login Works

- Hermes requests a device code fromauth.x.ai.
- You open the verification URL, sign in, enter the displayed code if prompted, and approve access.
- Hermes polls xAI until approval, then saves tokens to~/.hermes/auth.json.
- From then on, Hermes refreshes the access token in the background — you stay signed in until youhermes auth logout xai-oauth or revoke access from your xAI account settings.

## Checking Login Status
hermes doctor

The◆ Auth Providers section will show the current state of every provider, including xai-oauth.

## Switching Models
hermes model
# → Select "xAI Grok OAuth (SuperGrok / X Premium+)"
# → Pick from the model list (grok-4.6 is pinned to the top)

Or set the model directly:
hermes config set model.default grok-4.6
hermes config set model.provider xai-oauth

## Configuration Reference

After login,~/.hermes/config.yaml will contain:
model:
  default: grok-4.6
  provider: xai-oauth
  base_url: https://api.x.ai/v1

### Provider aliases

All of the following resolve toxai-oauth:
hermes --provider xai-oauth        # canonical
hermes --provider grok-oauth       # alias
hermes --provider x-ai-oauth       # alias
hermes --provider xai-grok-oauth   # alias

## Direct-to-xAI Tools (TTS / Image / Video / Transcription / X Search)

Once you're logged in via OAuth, every direct-to-xAI tool reuses the same bearer token automatically — there is no separate setup unless you'd rather use an API key.

To pick a backend for each tool:
hermes tools
# → Text-to-Speech       → "xAI TTS"
# → Image Generation     → "xAI Grok Imagine (image)"
# → Video Generation     → "xAI Grok Imagine"
# → X (Twitter) Search   → "xAI Grok OAuth (SuperGrok / X Premium+)"

If OAuth tokens are already stored, the picker confirms it and skips the credential prompt. If neither OAuth norXAI_API_KEY is set, the picker offers a 3-choice menu: OAuth login, paste API key, or skip.

Video generation is off by default

Thevideo_gen toolset is disabled by default. Enable it in hermes tools → 🎬 Video Generation (press space) before the agent can call video_generate. Otherwise the agent may fall back to the bundled ComfyUI skill, which is also tagged for video generation.

X search auto-enables when xAI credentials are present

Thex_search toolset auto-enables whenever xAI credentials (a SuperGrok / X Premium+ OAuth token or XAI_API_KEY) are configured. Disable explicitly via hermes tools → 🐦 X (Twitter) Search (press space) if you don't want this. The tool routes through xAI's built-in x_search Responses API — it works with either your SuperGrok / X Premium+ OAuth login or a paid XAI_API_KEY, and prefers OAuth when both are configured (uses your subscription quota instead of API spend). The tool schema is hidden from the model when no xAI credentials are configured, regardless of whether the toolset is enabled.

Chat | grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning | Non-reasoning variant 
Chat | grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309 | Multi-agent variant 
Image | grok-imagine-image | Default; ~5–10 s 
Image | grok-imagine-image-2.0 | Typography/layout-aware; strongest quality; ~10–20 s 
Image | grok-imagine-image-quality | Higher fidelity; ~10–20 s 
Video | grok-imagine-video | Text-to-video 
Video | grok-imagine-video-1.5-preview | Image-to-video; dated alias grok-imagine-video-1.5-2026-05-30 
TTS | (default voice) | xAI /v1/tts endpoint

### Token expired — not re-logging in automatically

Hermes refreshes the token before each session and again reactively on a 401. If refresh fails withinvalid_grant (the refresh token was revoked, or the account was rotated), Hermes surfaces a typed re-auth message instead of crashing.

### SessionProperties

Parameter | Type | Default | Description 
---|---|---|---

resumption | SessionResumption | None | Session resumption opt-in. Set enabled=True to cache conversation history for reconnection. 
replace | dict[str, str] | None | Pronunciation replacement map applied before TTS (e.g., {"Acme": "Ack-mee"}). 

### TurnDetection

Theturn_detection field in SessionProperties configures voice activity detection and turn management:

Parameter | Type | Default | Description 
---|---|---|---
type | Literal["server_vad"] | None | "server_vad" | Detection type: "server_vad" for automatic detection, None for manual control. 
threshold | float | None | VAD activation threshold (0.1–0.9). Higher values require louder audio. 
silence_duration_ms | int | None | Milliseconds of silence before the server ends the user turn. 
prefix_padding_ms | int | None | Audio (ms) included before detected speech start. 
idle_timeout_ms | int | None | Milliseconds of silence after assistant response before proactive check-in. 

### AudioConfiguration

Theaudio field in SessionProperties accepts an AudioConfiguration with input and output sub-configurations:

AudioInput (audio.input):

Parameter | Type | Default | Description 
---|---|---|---
format | AudioFormat | None | Input audio format. Supports PCMAudioFormat (configurable rate), PCMUAudioFormat (8kHz), or PCMAAudioFormat (8kHz). 
transcription | InputAudioTranscription | None | Transcription settings. Set model="grok-transcribe" for streaming user captions. 
transport | Literal["json", "binary"] | None | Wire path for input audio. 

AudioOutput (audio.output):

Parameter | Type | Default | Description 
---|---|---|---
format | AudioFormat | None | Output audio format. Same format options as input. 
speed | float | None | Playback speed multiplier (0.7–1.5). 
transport | Literal["json", "binary"] | None | Wire path for assistant audio. 

Grok PCM audio supports sample rates: 8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100, and 48000 Hz.

InputAudioTranscription (audio.input.transcription):

Parameter | Type | Default | Description 
---|---|---|---
model | str | None | Transcription model. Use "grok-transcribe" for streaming user captions. 
language_hint | str | None | BCP-47 language code to bias ASR (e.g., "en-US"). 
keyterms | list[str] | None | Domain terms to bias transcription (max 100 terms, ≤50 chars each). 

### Built-in Tools

Grok provides several built-in tools in addition to custom function tools:

Tool | Type | Description 
---|---|---
WebSearchTool | web_search | Search the web for current information 
XSearchTool | x_search | Search X (Twitter) for posts. Supports allowed_x_handles filter. 
FileSearchTool | file_search | Search uploaded document collections by vector_store_ids 
McpTool | mcp | Remote MCP tool configuration managed by xAI

### Basic Setup

# huggingface/transformers v5.24.0 Release v5.24.0

# Release v5.24.0

## New Model additions

### Inkling 2 Mini

Inkling 2 Mini is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is a smaller sibling of Inkling 2 Small, added in v5.23.0. It has 24 decoder layers instead of 48, and compensates with a looping mechanism in which layers 6 to 17 run three times. A learned message-passing mechanism mixes the residuals of the previous pass into the attention and mixture-of-experts inputs of each loop layer. The decoder has a hidden size of 2304 and routes each token to 8 of 128 experts. The image encoder, tokenizer and processor are the same as Inkling 2 Small's.

A research checkpoint (TML-d24-varloop-research) has the same architecture but supports a variable number of loop passes. Fewer passes are faster, and more passes improve quality. Both checkpoints contain NVFP4 and MXFP8 quantized layers, which are dequantized at load time.

- Add Inkling2 Mini (#51050) by @guarin

### Apertus 1.5

Apertus 1.5 is a multimodal model from the Swiss AI Initiative that accepts text, images and audio and generates text. It extends the Apertus language model with the EMU3.5 vision tokenizer for images and WavTokenizer for audio. The EMU3.5 tokenizer is an image-only VQGAN with the same encoder as Chameleon's, and it assigns codes by the largest inner product with the codebook. The media tokenizers turn images and audio into discrete tokens, which the language backbone processes alongside text in a shared input vocabulary. The output vocabulary contains only text tokens, so image and audio generation are not supported.

- Apertus 1.5: add model (#47662) by @RaphaelKreft

### WavTokenizer

WavTokenizer encodes 24 kHz mono audio into discrete tokens using a single codebook, at 40 or 75 tokens per second depending on the checkpoint, and reconstructs audio from those tokens.WavTokenizerModel encodes and decodes, and WavTokenizerEncoderModel only encodes. Speech, music/audio and unified checkpoints are available. The 40-token-per-second variant is the audio tokenizer of Apertus 1.5. Training the codec is not supported.

- Apertus 1.5: add model (#47662) by @RaphaelKreft

### Dory

Dory is a looped (latent-recurrent) language model from NVIDIA. It uses a normalized-GPT architecture with interleaved sliding-window and full attention layers. A shared block of layers is applied repeatedly, so Dory can spend more compute per token. The loop count can be changed at inference time on the same checkpoint to trade speed against quality.

- Add Dory model support (#50099) by @shan18

### HY4-VL

HY4-VL (Hunyuan V4 Vision-Language) combines the HYV4 mixture-of-experts text backbone with a vision encoder for image-text and video-text generation. It supports dynamic-resolution visual inputs and uses multimodal rotary position embeddings (mRoPE) to represent temporal and spatial positions. It builds on the Qwen2-VL design and shares its vision patch merger with HunYuan-VL.

- Add HY4-VL (#50877) by @vasqu

### Omnilingual ASR

Omnilingual ASR is a suite of multilingual speech-recognition models from Meta FAIR that covers more than 1,600 languages. Each model pairs a Wav2Vec2-style audio encoder with one of two heads:

- CTC (OmniASRForCTC): a linear projection to the vocabulary, decoded non-autoregressively with greedy CTC.

- Audio language model (OmniASRForConditionalGeneration): audio embeddings are projected into a Llama decoder that generates the transcription. It optionally takes a language code (e.g. "eng_Latn"), which generally improves transcription quality.

Both variants come in 300M, 1B, 3B and 7B sizes.

- Adding Omnilingual ASR models (#43265) by @ebezzam

### Lara Mini

Lara Mini is a multilingual base language model from Translated with 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters per token. It is a hybrid of linear-time recurrent layers, sliding-window attention and a few global attention layers, each followed by a fine-grained mixture of experts. The weights are released under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license (non-commercial use) in a gated repository.

- Add Lara Mini (#50819) by @ValeGian

### SarvamMLA

SarvamMLA is the architecture of Sarvam-105B, a 105B-parameter mixture-of-experts language model from Sarvam AI. It combines Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) with sparse MoE routing: 128 routed experts with 8 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. It uses sigmoid routing with group-based top-k selection and YaRN rotary embeddings for contexts up to 131K tokens. The architecture is the same as DeepSeek-V3, with a custom configuration.

- Add SarvamMLA model (sarvamai/sarvam-105b) (#44569) by @aashay-sarvam

### SarvamMoE

SarvamMoE is the architecture of Sarvam-30B, Sarvam AI's 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model. It uses grouped-query attention with QK normalization, and 128 routed experts with 6 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. The architecture is the same as GLM-4-MoE, so the auto classes load it with the GLM-4-MoE implementation and onlySarvamMoEConfig is specific to SarvamMoE.

- Add SarvamMoE (sarvamai/sarvam-30b) (#51023) by @hmellor

### EXAONE

EXAONE covers the EXAONE 3.0, EXAONE 3.5 and EXAONE Deep language models from LG AI Research. Their architecture is the same as Llama, so the auto classes load them withLlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM, and only ExaoneConfig is specific to EXAONE. The released checkpoints are renamed to the Llama names when loading and back when saving, so they no longer need trust_remote_code=True.

- Add EXAONE (#50966) by @hmellor

### Model updates

- Ling 3.1 Flash now loads natively throughBailingHybrid, like Ling 3.0 in v5.20.0 (#49737) by @icavan

- Beam gains aBeamForTokenClassification head (#50634) by @AymenKallala

## Breaking changes

### Cache renaming:past_key_values / cache_params → cache (#50585, #50730)

past_key_values and cache_params are renamed to cache across the library. The old names still work with a deprecation warning; see the dedicated section below.

- 🚨🚨 Renamepast_key_values/cache_params to cache (#50585) by @Cyrilvallez

- Bump minimal peft version for cache name compatibility (#50730) by @Cyrilvallez

Attention models used to call their cachepast_key_values, while Mamba-style and linear-attention models called it cache_params. Hybrid models therefore had to juggle two names for the same object. There is now a single name, cache, everywhere: model forward signatures, generate, prepare_inputs_for_generation, the masking utilities, and every ModelOutput.

# Before
outputs = model(input_ids, past_key_values=past_key_values, use_cache=True)
next_cache = outputs.past_key_values

# Now
outputs = model(input_ids, cache=cache, use_cache=True)
next_cache = outputs.cache
- Fully backward compatible for now:past_key_values= / cache_params= are renamed to cache automatically, with a one-time deprecation warning. Model forward and prepare_inputs_for_generation accept the old names until v5.40.0, and generate accepts them until v6.0.0. Passing both an old name and cache raises a ValueError.

- Outputs too:outputs.past_key_values, outputs.cache_params and outputs["past_key_values"] still return the cache. Output classes can also still be built with the old field names (e.g. CausalLMOutputWithPast(past_key_values=...)), so most remote-code models keep working unchanged.

- Custom code: models defined outside the library should rename their arguments tocache. Layers now call cache.update(key_states, value_states, layer_idx, kwargs=kwargs), so custom Cache subclasses that override update should accept the extra kwargs argument.

🚨peft>=0.22.0 is now required.

### Multimodal Outputs

Generative multimodal models now return shared output classes (MultimodalBaseModelOutputWithPast, MultimodalCausalLMOutputWithPast, and their MoE variants) instead of one output class per model. Code that checks for a model-specific output class should switch to these.

- 🚨 Multimodal Model Output for generative LMs (#50379) by @zucchini-nlp

modeling_attn_mask_utils.py has been removed. Every function in it had been deprecated in favor of transformers.masking_utils. Remote-code models that still import _prepare_4d_causal_attention_mask or AttentionMaskConverter from it must move to transformers.masking_utils.

### Other things

- Remove deprecated and unused older mask API file (#50728) by @Cyrilvallez

LayoutLMv3 (and the PP-DocLayoutV2 reading-order model that shares its code) now go through the attention interface, so SDPA and flex attention are supported. The relative position bias is built once per forward pass and passed to attention asposition_bias.

- 🚨 LayoutLMv3: support SDPA through the attention interface, build the relative position bias once (#50688) by @14H034160212

## Cache

Beyond the rename, this release adds static-cache support to assisted decoding and fixesgenerate with flex attention and a static cache. StaticCache now allocates values with the value states' dtype, and the cache is kept under activation checkpointing when gradients are off. The is_linear / is_croppable properties are fixed for hybrid linear/full-attention models, BigBird block-sparse decoding works with a KV cache, and KV sharing is restored for the Gemma 4 assistants.

- Support static cache in assisted decoding (#49415) by @jiqing-feng
- Simplify cache handling in generate (#50910) by @Cyrilvallez
- Fix generate with flex attention and a static cache (#50864) by @tarekziade
- Allocate the StaticCache values with the value states' dtype (#49554) by @qgallouedec
- Keep the cache under activation checkpointing when gradients are off (#50890) by @qgallouedec
- [cache] Fix is_linear property to correctly remove hybrid layers (#51030) by @Cyrilvallez
- Fix is_croppable property for mixed linear-full attention classes (#51028) by @Cyrilvallez
- Fix BigBird block-sparse decoding with a KV cache (#49984) by @jiqing-feng
- fix(gemma4): Restore

# Release v5.24.0

## New Model additions

### Inkling 2 Mini

Inkling 2 Mini is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is a smaller sibling of Inkling 2 Small, added in v5.23.0. It has 24 decoder layers instead of 48, and compensates with a looping mechanism in which layers 6 to 17 run three times. A learned message-passing mechanism mixes the residuals of the previous pass into the attention and mixture-of-experts inputs of each loop layer. The decoder has a hidden size of 2304 and routes each token to 8 of 128 experts. The image encoder, tokenizer and processor are the same as Inkling 2 Small's.

A research checkpoint (TML-d24-varloop-research) has the same architecture but supports a variable number of loop passes. Fewer passes are faster, and more passes improve quality. Both checkpoints contain NVFP4 and MXFP8 quantized layers, which are dequantized at load time.

- Add Inkling2 Mini (#51050) by @guarin

### Apertus 1.5

Apertus 1.5 is a multimodal model from the Swiss AI Initiative that accepts text, images and audio and generates text. It extends the Apertus language model with the EMU3.5 vision tokenizer for images and WavTokenizer for audio. The EMU3.5 tokenizer is an image-only VQGAN with the same encoder as Chameleon's, and it assigns codes by the largest inner product with the codebook. The media tokenizers turn images and audio into discrete tokens, which the language backbone processes alongside text in a shared input vocabulary. The output vocabulary contains only text tokens, so image and audio generation are not supported.

- Apertus 1.5: add model (#47662) by @RaphaelKreft

### WavTokenizer

WavTokenizer encodes 24 kHz mono audio into discrete tokens using a single codebook, at 40 or 75 tokens per second depending on the checkpoint, and reconstructs audio from those tokens.WavTokenizerModel encodes and decodes, and WavTokenizerEncoderModel only encodes. Speech, music/audio and unified checkpoints are available. The 40-token-per-second variant is the audio tokenizer of Apertus 1.5. Training the codec is not supported.

- Apertus 1.5: add model (#47662) by @RaphaelKreft

### Dory

Dory is a looped (latent-recurrent) language model from NVIDIA. It uses a normalized-GPT architecture with interleaved sliding-window and full attention layers. A shared block of layers is applied repeatedly, so Dory can spend more compute per token. The loop count can be changed at inference time on the same checkpoint to trade speed against quality.

- Add Dory model support (#50099) by @shan18

### HY4-VL

HY4-VL (Hunyuan V4 Vision-Language) combines the HYV4 mixture-of-experts text backbone with a vision encoder for image-text and video-text generation. It supports dynamic-resolution visual inputs and uses multimodal rotary position embeddings (mRoPE) to represent temporal and spatial positions. It builds on the Qwen2-VL design and shares its vision patch merger with HunYuan-VL.

- Add HY4-VL (#50877) by @vasqu

### Omnilingual ASR

Omnilingual ASR is a suite of multilingual speech-recognition models from Meta FAIR that covers more than 1,600 languages. Each model pairs a Wav2Vec2-style audio encoder with one of two heads:

- CTC (OmniASRForCTC): a linear projection to the vocabulary, decoded non-autoregressively with greedy CTC.

- Audio language model (OmniASRForConditionalGeneration): audio embeddings are projected into a Llama decoder that generates the transcription. It optionally takes a language code (e.g. "eng_Latn"), which generally improves transcription quality.

Both variants come in 300M, 1B, 3B and 7B sizes.

- Adding Omnilingual ASR models (#43265) by @ebezzam

### Lara Mini

Lara Mini is a multilingual base language model from Translated with 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters per token. It is a hybrid of linear-time recurrent layers, sliding-window attention and a few global attention layers, each followed by a fine-grained mixture of experts. The weights are released under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license (non-commercial use) in a gated repository.

- Add Lara Mini (#50819) by @ValeGian

### SarvamMLA

SarvamMLA is the architecture of Sarvam-105B, a 105B-parameter mixture-of-experts language model from Sarvam AI. It combines Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) with sparse MoE routing: 128 routed experts with 8 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. It uses sigmoid routing with group-based top-k selection and YaRN rotary embeddings for contexts up to 131K tokens. The architecture is the same as DeepSeek-V3, with a custom configuration.

- Add SarvamMLA model (sarvamai/sarvam-105b) (#44569) by @aashay-sarvam

### SarvamMoE

SarvamMoE is the architecture of Sarvam-30B, Sarvam AI's 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model. It uses grouped-query attention with QK normalization, and 128 routed experts with 6 active per token, plus 1 shared expert. The architecture is the same as GLM-4-MoE, so the auto classes load it with the GLM-4-MoE implementation and onlySarvamMoEConfig is specific to SarvamMoE.

- Add SarvamMoE (sarvamai/sarvam-30b) (#51023) by @hmellor

### EXAONE

EXAONE covers the EXAONE 3.0, EXAONE 3.5 and EXAONE Deep language models from LG AI Research. Their architecture is the same as Llama, so the auto classes load them withLlamaModel and LlamaForCausalLM, and only ExaoneConfig is specific to EXAONE. The released checkpoints are renamed to the Llama names when loading and back when saving, so they no longer need trust_remote_code=True.

- Add EXAONE (#50966) by @hmellor

### Model updates

- Ling 3.1 Flash now loads natively throughBailingHybrid, like Ling 3.0 in v5.20.0 (#49737) by @icavan

- Beam gains aBeamForTokenClassification head (#50634) by @AymenKallala

## Breaking changes

### Cache renaming:past_key_values / cache_params → cache (#50585, #50730)

past_key_values and cache_params are renamed to cache across the library. The old names still work with a deprecation warning; see the dedicated section below.

- 🚨🚨 Renamepast_key_values/cache_params to cache (#50585) by @Cyrilvallez

- Bump minimal peft version for cache name compatibility (#50730) by @Cyrilvallez

Attention models used to call their cachepast_key_values, while Mamba-style and linear-attention models called it cache_params. Hybrid models therefore had to juggle two names for the same object. There is now a single name, cache, everywhere: model forward signatures, generate, prepare_inputs_for_generation, the masking utilities, and every ModelOutput.

# Before
outputs = model(input_ids, past_key_values=past_key_values, use_cache=True)
next_cache = outputs.past_key_values

# Now
outputs = model(input_ids, cache=cache, use_cache=True)
next_cache = outputs.cache
- Fully backward compatible for now:past_key_values= / cache_params= are renamed to cache automatically, with a one-time deprecation warning. Model forward and prepare_inputs_for_generation accept the old names until v5.40.0, and generate accepts them until v6.0.0. Passing both an old name and cache raises a ValueError.

- Outputs too:outputs.past_key_values, outputs.cache_params and outputs["past_key_values"] still return the cache. Output classes can also still be built with the old field names (e.g. CausalLMOutputWithPast(past_key_values=...)), so most remote-code models keep working unchanged.

- Custom code: models defined outside the library should rename their arguments tocache. Layers now call cache.update(key_states, value_states, layer_idx, kwargs=kwargs), so custom Cache subclasses that override update should accept the extra kwargs argument.

🚨peft>=0.22.0 is now required.

### Multimodal Outputs

Generative multimodal models now return shared output classes (MultimodalBaseModelOutputWithPast, MultimodalCausalLMOutputWithPast, and their MoE variants) instead of one output class per model. Code that checks for a model-specific output class should switch to these.

- 🚨 Multimodal Model Output for generative LMs (#50379) by @zucchini-nlp

modeling_attn_mask_utils.py has been removed. Every function in it had been deprecated in favor of transformers.masking_utils. Remote-code models that still import _prepare_4d_causal_attention_mask or AttentionMaskConverter from it must move to transformers.masking_utils.

### Other things

- Remove deprecated and unused older mask API file (#50728) by @Cyrilvallez

LayoutLMv3 (and the PP-DocLayoutV2 reading-order model that shares its code) now go through the attention interface, so SDPA and flex attention are supported. The relative position bias is built once per forward pass and passed to attention asposition_bias.

- 🚨 LayoutLMv3: support SDPA through the attention interface, build the relative position bias once (#50688) by @14H034160212

## Cache

Beyond the rename, this release adds static-cache support to assisted decoding and fixesgenerate with flex attention and a static cache. StaticCache now allocates values with the value states' dtype, and the cache is kept under activation checkpointing when gradients are off. The is_linear / is_croppable properties are fixed for hybrid linear/full-attention models, BigBird block-sparse decoding works with a KV cache, and KV sharing is restored for the Gemma 4 assistants.

- Support static cache in assisted decoding (#49415) by @jiqing-feng
- Simplify cache handling in generate (#50910) by @Cyrilvallez
- Fix generate with flex attention and a static cache (#50864) by @tarekziade
- Allocate the StaticCache values with the value states' dtype (#49554) by @qgallouedec
- Keep the cache under activation checkpointing when gradients are off (#50890) by @qgallouedec
- [cache] Fix is_linear property to correctly remove hybrid layers (#51030) by @Cyrilvallez
- Fix is_croppable property for mixed linear-full attention classes (#51028) by @Cyrilvallez
- Fix BigBird block-sparse decoding with a KV cache (#49984) by @jiqing-feng
- fix(gemma4): Restore KV sharing f

# Introducing Clef: Cloudflare's first open-source decision models, now on Workers AI
import { TypeScriptExample } from "~/components";

Meet@cf/cloudflare/clef and @cf/cloudflare/clef-flash, the first models trained by the Cloudflare Workers AI team, available on Workers AI today.

Clef is a decision model, in the same family as Typesafe's Jev. Instead of generating text, it reads an input state and a set of typed questions, then returns a probability for every allowed answer. Your agent gets a structured decision it can act on immediately, for example: route the ticket, block the request, or escalate to a human. There is no free-form output to parse and no reasoning tokens to wait for.

Both models are hosted on Workers AI as Clef and Clef-flash. We are also open-sourcing the weights under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face: Clef and Clef-flash. Read the launch blog post for the full story, including how we trained them.

We are also launching a reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning service to help you tune Clef for your own workloads. Sign up to work with us as a design partner.

## Built for the hot path

Clef is designed to be fast so decisions come back in milliseconds. Across our 43 benchmark runs, we achieved speeds where Clef is 2.5x faster than Jev at the median, and Clef-flash 13x faster.

Latency | Clef | Clef-flash | Jev 
---|---|---|---
Median | 209.3 ms | 38.8 ms | 524.1 ms 
p95 | 238.6 ms | 122.4 ms | 536.0 ms 

Hosting on Workers AI adds to that speed. Requests run on GPUs across Cloudflare's network, running close to your users, so the network round trip stays short. You can put Clef directly in the request path of your agent, then hand off to an LLM on Workers AI to take action.

## Leading the benchmarks

Across 10 decision benchmarks, a Clef model scores highest on 7, ahead of Jev and other open decision models. A few highlights:

Benchmark | Clef | Clef-flash | Jev 
---|---|---|---
BFCL (case exact) | 98.47 | 98.76 | 95.75 
BANKING77 (macro-F1) | 94.20 | 90.93 | 79.74 
CLINC150+OOS (macro-F1) | 97.43 | 66.77 | 89.27 
Home appliances (case exact) | 82.95 | 97.73 | 52.27 

On Typesafe's own workflow evals, Clef beats Jev in 3 of 4 areas: invoice processing, customer service, and security incidents. The full results are on the Hugging Face model card.

## Drop-in compatible with Jev

Model | Size | Best for | Context window 
---|---|---|---
@cf/cloudflare/clef27B | Highest-precision decisions | 64K tokens 
@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash9B | Latency-critical, hot-path decisions | 64K tokens 

Clef follows the System One API, so you can switch an existing Jev integration to Clef by changing the endpoint and model. Ask up to 64 questions per request, in three types:

- noul: A yes/no question. Returns the probability that the answer is yes.
- choice: Pick one option from a set you define. Returns the chosen option, a probability per option, and a confidence value.
- score: Rate against an ordered rubric. Returns a probability-weighted score and a probability per level.

const response = await env.AI.run("@cf/cloudflare/clef", {
	model: "clef",
	state: "Checkout has been failing for every customer for the last hour.",
	questions: {
		urgent: {
			type: "noul",
			instructions: "Is this support request urgent?",
		},
		team: {
			type: "choice",
			instructions: "Which team should handle this request?",
			criteria: {
				billing: "Payments, invoices, and refunds",
				technical: "Outages, errors, and configuration",
				sales: "Plans and upgrades",
			},
		},
	},
});

// response.answers.urgent.noul -> probability the request is urgent
// response.answers.team.choice -> highest-probability team

## What you can build with decision models

- Support triage: Decide whether a ticket is urgent and which team owns it, then route it without a human in the loop.
- Threat intelligence: Classify a website by category. Paired with Browser Run, Clef fetched, rendered, and classified a domain in 2.2 seconds, compared to 4.7 seconds forgpt-oss-120b in the same workflow.
- Trust and safety: Score user submissions against your own policy rubric and act on the probability.
- Agent guardrails: Let an agent check "should I take this action?" in tens of milliseconds before calling a tool.
- Visual classification: Pass up to four images alongside the state. Unlike text-only decision models, Clef has a vision encoder.

## Get started

Use Clef through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. You can also use AI Gateway with these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Clef model page, the Clef-flash model page, and pricing.

# Supported models, regions, and versions for model router

This article is the reference for the models that model router in Microsoft Foundry can route to, the regions where you can use it, and how long each model router version is supported. Use it to choose models for a model subset, confirm that your region is supported, and plan version moves. Other model router articles link here instead of repeating these lists.

- As of November 18, 2026, model router version2025-11-18 routes across 45 models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft AI, xAI, DeepSeek, Meta, and Fireworks. Eight of them are new in November 2026.
- You don't deploy the underlying models yourself, except Claude models. Deploy each Claude model in the same Foundry resource before model router can route to it.
- Model router routes to the Fireworks models only when Fireworks is enabled for your Azure subscription. See Fireworks models.
- Model router is available in 32 regions for Global Standard deployments, and 23 of them also offer Data Zone Standard. Auto (model router without a deployment) is available in all 32.
- Each model router version has its own retirement date. Model router itself isn't retiring.

## Supported models

By default, a model router deployment routes across every model in this table that's available in your region. Auto does the same, unless an admin sets Auto's models for the resource. To route across fewer models, choose a model subset.

When you list models in a deployment request (properties.routing.models) or in Auto's resource settings (properties.instant.routing.models), use the exact format, name, and version values from this table. Per-request controls (routing_config.models) take the name only.

### Claude models

A model router deployment routes to a Claude model only when both of these conditions are true:

- The Claude model is deployed in the same Foundry resource as your model router deployment, as a Global Standard deployment of the version in the preceding table. Model router doesn't use other versions, such as the Azure-hosted version2 that the Foundry portal selects by default. To deploy one, see Deploy and use Claude models.
- If your model router deployment uses a model subset, the subset includes the Claude model.

These Claude versions are available only as Global Standard deployments, so a Data Zone Standard model router deployment doesn't route to Claude models.

Auto can route to a Claude model when your resource has a deployment of that model. Only Claude models answer Messages API requests.

In a request, setmodel to your model router deployment name or to auto. Setting model to a Claude model name doesn't select that model through model router. For the steps, see Add Claude models.

### Fireworks models

Model router routes to the Fireworks models (FW-GLM-5.3, FW-GLM-5.3-Flash, and FW-Kimi-K3) only when Fireworks is enabled for your Azure subscription. To enable it, a subscription admin reviews the terms and registers the Fireworks.EnableDeploy preview feature. Without it, model router doesn't route to these models. For steps, see Enable Fireworks on Foundry.

### How the model pool changes

New models are added to version2025-11-18 without changing the version name. Retired models are removed. What's new in model router lists each change.

- If your deployment uses the full pool, new models are included and retired models drop out with no action from you.
- If your deployment uses a model subset, new models aren't added until you add them. If a model in your subset retires, replace it with a supported model. See Route to a subset of models.

### List the current model pool programmatically

The Foundry models API returns the current pool for each model router version in a region. The following Azure CLI command returns theformat, name, and version of each model in the version 2025-11-18 pool for East US 2:
SUBSCRIPTION_ID=$(az account show --query id --output tsv)

az rest --method get \
  --url "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/$SUBSCRIPTION_ID/providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/locations/eastus2/models?api-version=2025-06-01" \
  --query "value[?model.name=='model-router' && model.version=='2025-11-18'] | [0].model.capabilities.models" \
  --output tsv

The command returns a JSON array with one entry for each model. The output starts like this example:
[{"format":"OpenAI","name":"gpt-4o","version":"2024-11-20"},{"format":"OpenAI","name":"gpt-4o-mini","version":"2024-07-18"}, ...]

The array lists every model in the version's pool. It can include models that model router can't use in that region. To check a model, send a request to Auto, or to a deployment that uses the full pool, withrouting_config.models set to only that model. HTTP 400 with invalid_routing_models means that model router can't use the model in your region.

## Supported regions

Model router version2025-11-18 supports the following regions. A check mark (✅) means that the deployment type is available. A hyphen (-) means that it isn't. Auto (model router without a deployment) is available in all 32 regions and always processes data as Global Standard.

# Language model library

Source: https://docs.cognite.com/cdf/atlas_ai/references/atlas_ai_agent_language_models

Detailed reference of available language models in Atlas AI, including stable, legacy, and retired models with release and retirement dates.

Choose the right model based on your requirements for speed, quality, and context length. The availability of language models depends on your preferred cloud vendor and the location of your Cognite Data Fusion (CDF) project.

Cognite continuously refreshes language models with newer and more capable models for building agents. As part of this process, Cognite retires older models.

These terms describe lifecycle stages and important dates for language models available in Atlas AI:

Stable model: A released model version supported for production use. Stable models include a retirement date when Cognite Atlas AI will no longer support them.

Latest stable model: The most current version within the model family, recommended for new agents or agents in development. Use this model when migrating from older versions.

Legacy stable model: An older model version that the latest stable model has replaced. While Atlas AI still supports legacy models, migrate to the latest model to access new features and improvements.

Recommended upgrade: The latest stable model to migrate to for improved performance and additional features.

Retired model: A model version that Atlas AI has permanently deactivated after reaching its retirement date. Atlas AI no longer supports retired models. If you don't migrate agents using retired models before the retirement date, they automatically upgrade to the latest stable model.

When an opportunity is ready, teams can send it to coding agents, including Codex, with a technical plan and acceptance criteria (OpenAI). Amplitude's own page describes the loop as designing new builds, orchestrating coding agents to generate pull requests and running experiments to validate impact (Amplitude (official statement)).

In a sample of 100 session replays, 80 users typed their own questions and only 12 selected a suggestion card (OpenAI). Wave proposed personalizing the cards, and after a brief review the team handed the work to a coding agent and A/B tested the change (OpenAI). For solution wireframes, OpenAI's image model scored 80.3 out of 100 against 63.9 for another image model across 15 opportunities (OpenAI).

Amplitude said most teams send bug fixes straight to coding agents, while new features and bigger bets get a human review (OpenAI). Among customer-launched experiments, flags and guides, one in four went live the same day Wave surfaced the opportunity, half in under four days and two in three within a week (OpenAI). Amplitude's page cites a PixAI case in which an out-of-credits tooltip led to publishing rising nearly 10% and Day 1 retention rising 3% over control (Amplitude (official statement)).

Amplitude lists requirements for Wave: an eligible Growth or Enterprise plan, meaningful Product Analytics and Session Replay data, and a business goal to improve (Amplitude (official statement)). # Muse产品负责人分享：从树莓派周末实验到上线，整个过程打磨了七个月

这一期，我们听的是 Lenny's Podcast 对 Mona Sarantakos（Meta Superintelligence Labs产品副总裁） 的访谈。

【这期讲什么】
Muse 是 App Store 排名第一的应用，也可以说是有史以来增长最快的 AI 消费级产品。Mona Sarantakos 从第一天起就负责它的产品工作。她是 Meta Superintelligence Labs 的产品副总裁，也是 Meta 的资深员工，任职已有 10 年，拥有超过 20 年的产品经理经验。这是她第一次接受播客采访。

【你会听到】

- 一个周末在 Raspberry Pi 上使用 OpenClaw，如何最终诞生了 Muse
- 尽管 Muse 比大多数竞争对手更早启动，为什么还是等了七个月才发布
- Nat Friedman、Alex Wang 和 Mark Zuckerberg 如何分别在这款产品上留下自己的印记
- 团队如何利用“智能体蜂群”大规模挖掘用户洞察
- 团队中没有人预料到的使用场景
- 真正能够推动 AI 智能体激活的两个杠杆
- 如今 Mona 在 PM 身上最看重的一点

我是 Felix，在中美经营一家 AI 技术公司。
想共同探索 AI 机会，或者想加入我的团队做有意思的事，欢迎来找我：

## 本期看点

AI 从整集转写里归纳的，不是节目方的宣传语

最值得听的

Mona拆解Muse为何坚持打磨七个月：自建评测标准、每加一个功能就堵一条攻击路径，信任是上线前提。

别处听不到的

董事会前一小时原型突然坏掉，团队赶在开会前五分钟修好，Mona说否则Muse可能根本不会诞生。

最打动人的

两个用户的Muse在群聊里从可爱闲聊到暴露隐私、再到吵架，最后还得坐下来“弹劾”，团队由此意识到边界。

## 为什么值得听

AI 读完整集转写后给出的推荐理由

Muse产品负责人Mona第一次上播客，讲了一个树莓派周末实验如何变成App Store榜首产品。她还原了董事会前一小时原型突然坏掉、赶在开会前五分钟修好的惊险时刻，也讲了那只差点被企业logo替换的毛绒玩具Jolly是怎么被团队“用尸体挡下来”的。购物意外成为最大使用场景、两个Muse在群聊里吵起来还得互相弹劾，这些内部故事别处听不到。

## 本期概要

由 AI 从整集转写生成，是创作者说明之外的补充

Meta超级智能实验室产品副总裁Mona Sarantakos讲述Muse从树莓派周末实验到上线App Store榜首的七个月历程。她回顾了Nat Friedman的一条消息如何触发整个项目、团队为何坚持打磨七个月才上线、Mark Zuckerberg和Alex Wang在产品中的角色、毛绒玩具Jolly差点被砍掉又留下的经过，以及购物意外成为最大使用场景。她还谈到智能体蜂群如何帮助评测、主聊天与侧边聊天的争议、两个Muse聊天引发的隐私边界问题，以及PM角色在AI时代从写文档转向产品品味与判断的变化。

## 章节

点一章从那里开始播 · 与上面创作者标的时间点各自独立

00:03

开场：一个周末实验引出的产品

主持人介绍Mona Sarantakos的身份与Muse的爆发式增长，用预告片方式点出购物场景意外走红、小团队用智能体蜂群找问题等看点。

02:37

从一条消息到正式团队

Mona讲述Nat Friedman发来OpenClaw消息后，她用树莓派搭环境、整个周末沉浸其中，周一收到学校简报后决定加入。团队先做实验和原型，直到二月才确定值得推进。

09:07

为什么花了七个月才上线

Mona把过程分为想清楚产品、打磨可靠性安全性与安全防护、扩大内测三个阶段。团队自建评测标准，每加一个功能就打开新攻击路径，坚持信任是必需品。

13:27

爪子就是法则与梦之队的分工

Mona解释“爪子就是法则”口号的由来，并讲述Nat Friedman深度参与安全架构、Alex Wang负责模型并推动上线、Mark Zuckerberg把团队从任务思维拉向对齐思维。

17:30

Jolly：差点被企业logo替换的毛绒玩具

Jolly从Alex Cornell用提示词生成的小圆球，一路变成产品核心符号。团队多次想拿掉它，Mark也反对替换，最终在发布前一周拍板留下。Mona提炼出品牌该淡出、产品原则要先定的经验。

25:37

购物成了最大的意外场景

团队原本看好效率、健康和理财，购物却意外成为最主要使用场景。Mona讲述工程师Christine的购物bug报告、自己收到七个包裹的经历，以及智能体如何改变购物决策。

32:18

智能体蜂群与评测体系

团队用智能体蜂群收集多轮对话数据、生成合成数据输入评测。评测超过一百项，涵盖安全、能力、行为和使用场景，系统提示词必须人工手写。Mona强调评测要培养对用户痛苦的共情。

38:32

激活难题：口碑比广告有用

Mona说头号问题是用户觉得已经有聊天机器人了。最有效的是口碑——一位妈妈现场演示让两人当场下载。团队做“想法”选项卡帮用户发出第一条提示词，并针对不同用户分层引导。

45:46

聊天气泡与主聊天的争议决定

团队放弃大画布路线选择聊天气泡，希望像消息服务一样自然，但随之而来的是消息拆分等一连串问题。主聊天与侧边聊天在内部引发两极反馈，最终保留侧边聊天但共享上下文。

50:41

# 【專訪】Meta Muse 產品負責人 Mona Sarantakos：AI 代理人寧可晚上市也不能失去信任

名人訪談簡介

Muse 是 Meta 推出的 AI 代理人，能替人收信，排行程，上網買東西。執行長馬克·祖克柏（Mark Zuckerberg）暗示，它是史上成長最快的 AI 消費產品。負責它的產品主管 Mona Sarantakos 在 Meta 待了十年，幾乎從不上節目。主持人 Lenny Rachitsky 這次當面問她：別家助理幾個月就上市，Muse 為什麼花了七個月？

每天精選 6 則要聞、一則產業名人訪談，五分鐘跟上。

Mona Sarantakos 說，AI 代理人寧可晚上市，也不能先失去信任。可是 AI 一天一變，晚幾個月不就把市場讓給對手？她的答案，落在代理人手裡握著的東西上。她也談到產品經理現在最該有的能力，以及 Meta 的商標為什麼得從產品裡退場。

## ◎信任是必須的：出一次大包，用戶就不會再用

Rachitsky 指出，其他 AI 助理從構想到上市只要幾個月，Muse 卻花了七個月。Sarantakos 說，春天時產品就大致能從頭跑到尾。真正耗掉時間的是三件事：穩定性，安全和資安。團隊內部有句口號，意思是信任是必須的。她說，團隊的門檻一直訂得非常高。

她的理由一層接一層。這個產品握有你的私人資料，還能替你下單買東西。太早上市又出一堆問題，大家就不會再信這個代理人。她說：「If you don't trust the agent, you're never going to use it.」（不信任這個代理人，你就永遠不會用它。）業界現成的評測標準不夠用，團隊只好自己訂一套更高的門檻。

她舉瀏覽器當例子。Muse 起初不能上網，加了瀏覽器，一整批新的資安破口就跟著冒出來。每加一個關鍵功能，就得先把新開的門全部關上。前 GitHub 執行長 Nat Friedman 也親自參與設計一道哨兵機制，在核心代理人之外多加一層防線。上市前，團隊先給員工用，再找外部測試者，用戶一批比一批多。

她丈夫前幾天也問她，別家代理人紛紛推出，會不會後悔沒早點上市？她說一樣都不會改，到現在 Muse 還沒出過災難性的問題。她也承認，整個領域還太早，有太多連自己都不知道的風險，產品永遠不會完美。晚上市讓出了多少市場，她沒有給數字。

## ◎產品經理最重要的能力，變成品味

七個月守住的門檻，最後也落在產品經理身上。Sarantakos 當了二十多年產品經理，以前得寫完整規格書，祈禱每個例外都想到。現在不是工程師也能用 AI 做出雛形，大家拿著實物討論，隔天就能改方向。她說，AI 讓粗製濫造的產品太容易推出去，產品經理要替用戶發聲，守住上線水準。她面試產品經理，最看重的就是品味。

## ◎代理人屬於用戶，Meta 的商標要退場

守住信任，也包括讓用戶覺得代理人屬於自己。App 頂端那隻叫 Jolly 的布偶，原本只是設計師 Alex Cornell 做雛形時放的臨時角色。Sarantakos 說它像團隊的蟑螂：每隔幾個月就有人說不能頂著布偶上市，它卻怎麼都死不了。她說，跟這麼私人的東西對話，最不想看到企業商標，代理人替你工作，Meta 得淡出。最後祖克柏和團隊拍板留下它。

回到那個問題：晚幾個月，會不會把市場讓給對手？Sarantakos 的說法是，代理人只要出一次大包，用戶就不會回來，所以她寧可先把信任做到。接下來可以觀察 Muse 離開手機 App：她說它很快該出現在眼鏡和 charm 這類裝置上。她也想讓用戶不必再像照顧電子雞一樣看顧代理人。

重要發言 KEY QUOTES 點時間碼即在此播放

[03:00]

Mona Sarantakos

Nat Friedman 傳訊說自己在試用 OpenClaw，要團隊趕快跟上。她原本在半年計畫裡寫，這類產品大概要到 2026 年底或 2027 年才會成熟。

[04:00]

Mona Sarantakos

買不到 Mac Mini，改用丈夫的 Raspberry Pi 架設，整個週末都在跟代理人對話。週一早上收到它整理的孩子學校週報，讓她決定投入。

[09:00]

Mona Sarantakos

主持人問為何花七個月才上市。她說耗時在穩定性，安全與資安，並提出內部口號 trust is a must。

[19:00]

Mona Sarantakos

描述 Nat Friedman，汪滔（Alexandr Wang），祖克柏各自的角色，包括設計核心代理人之外的哨兵機制，以及第一個 Muse Spark 模型的代理能力超出預期。

[23:00]

Mona Sarantakos

Jolly 角色的由來：取名自設計師對女兒的暱稱，多次差點被拿掉，最後因為不想讓企業商標破壞私人感而留下。

[32:00]

Mona Sarantakos

她沒料到購物會成為熱門用途，原本押注的家庭自動化反而沒那麼紅。團隊因此改建購物相關的評測。

[47:00]

Mona Sarantakos

談用戶啟用：最有效的是口碑。一位媽媽把手機傳給其他家長看，當場就有兩人下載，廣告則做不到這種效果。

[65:00]

Mona Sarantakos

說產品經理的門檻已經改變，產品品味成為最重要的能力，要能擋下 AI 做出的粗製濫造產品。

Invesco QQQ Trust ETF QQQ -5.67% ▼, which tracks the Nasdaq-100 index (NDX), closed 5.67% lower on Friday at $608.45. Again, Anthropic’s ANT -8.50% ▼ record Nasdaq debut on Thursday failed to reassure investors about the AI trade. Overall, Friday marked another bruising session for the entire U.S. stock market.

The chipmakers highlighted above rank among QQQ’s top holdings. Some of the stocks traded slightly higher in after-hours trading.

## Why Chip Stocks Sold Off on Friday

Beyond general market pressure, company-specific updates also weighed on chip stocks Friday.

- Nvidia shares NVDA -14.01% ▼ plunged 14.01% to $125.53. This followed reports that the U.S. securities watchdog is investigating the chipmaker’s accounting practices. This marks an escalation in the controversy facing the company. It follows a Chinese spy scandal that forced the dramatic exit of its longtime CEO, Jensen Huang, last week.
- Advanced Micro Devices shares AMD -13.25% ▼ dropped by 13.25% to $424.39. Shares in the chipmaker tumbled for a second day after a short-seller report. The report alleged that Chinese server maker IEIT Systems continued to receive updated AMD firmware despite being placed on the U.S. trade blacklist in March 2025. The report also flagged AMD’s financial exposure to its AI clients through leases and loan guarantees.
- Micron shares MU -13.89% ▼ plunged 13.89% to $594.51. This followed a report that warned that major Chinese cloud providers are likely to cut orders for enterprise solid-state drives in 2027. Nvidia’s ongoing leadership crisis also contributed to the sell-off.

# Partnership brings sovereign AI infrastructure to Europe

### Dublin, Ireland and Gilbert, Az

Armada, the Sovereign SI Infrastructure company, and Johnson Controls have partnered to start production at Galleon Forge Two, Armada’s first European manufacturing operation, located within a Johnson Controls facility in Dublin. It is the second Galleon Forge established at a Johnson Controls facility, following Galleon Forge One in Gilbert, Arizona, USA.

Together, the two sites expand Armada's manufacturing footprint and mark the start of continuous production of sovereign computing infrastructure in Europe. The companies marked the milestone with the completion of the first Dublin-built Leviathan, a multi-megawatt-scale modular data centre headed to Fossefall in Norway. Europe's first Leviathan was engineered, integrated, and tested entirely at Galleon Forge Two — proof that sovereign AI infrastructure for Europe can now be built in Europe.

Leviathan combines Armada's sovereign computing infrastructure and software with Johnson Controls differentiated thermal management technology and industrial-scale manufacturing capabilities. The Johnson Controls thermal portfolio spans the end-to-end thermal chain, including coolant distribution units, chillers, and building controls, and supports high-density compute with zero-water cooling technologies designed to reduce energy use and noise.

#### A manufacturing model built to expand

Galleon Forge Two follows Galleon Forge One at the Johnson Controls manufacturing site in Gilbert, Arizona, where continuous production is expected to begin in early 2027 across up to 400,000 square feet, supporting more than 500 jobs with additional roles across the domestic supply chain. Further manufacturing expansion is planned at a Johnson Controls site in Edmonton, Canada. The Galleon Forge model is designed to be anchored by any nation or region that wants sovereign AI infrastructure built at home, with local jobs, a local supply chain, and capacity that stays under local control.

Galleon Forge Two is located at a Johnson Controls manufacturing site in Dublin, Ireland, spanning 90,000 square feet and is supported by approximately 700 Johnson Controls engineers, technicians and other skilled workers, with additional roles across the European supply chain. For European governments and enterprises, the implications go beyond capacity: the infrastructure supporting their AI no longer has to be imported or rented. It is manufactured in Europe, owned by customers, and operated on their terms.

"The speed of the sovereign AI revolution requires a new approach to meet demand,” said Dan Wright, Co-founder and CEO of Armada. "The Galleon Forge model keeps producing, and it’s designed to keep expanding. We can now deliver to any nation or organisation that needs advanced computing infrastructure manufactured within its own borders — owned and controlled on its own terms."

“We’ve been building modular infrastructure for nearly two decades. What’s different today is the scale, density and speed AI demands,” said Austin Domenici, President, Global Data Center Solutions, Johnson Controls. “With Armada, we’re combining that experience with our thermal expertise and manufacturing scale to complete more of the complex integration work in the factory and bring compute online faster and more predictably.”

Leviathan runs on the Armada Platform, which manages power, cooling, and compute across every unit and runs the latest open-source or proprietary models. Customers own the infrastructure and control every layer, with no dependence on an external cloud. As part of the Armada Sovereign SI Grid, Leviathans run as one fleet, so critical workloads never depend on a single site.

#### Early deployments in Norway and Australia

Fossefall has placed an initial order for five Leviathan modular data centres totaling more than 9 MW, beginning with the unit completed today, with delivery of all five scheduled by the first quarter of 2027. Finding partners in Europe was particularly important for their vision of sovereignty.

"Europe needs more advanced computing infrastructure, and the focus now needs to be on getting projects built,” said Øyvind L. Vesterdal, CEO of Fossefall. “Working with Armada and Johnson Controls gives us a more standardised and modular approach to deployment. This can help shorten timelines and make projects easier to develop in close cooperation with local communities. With access to clean energy, political stability and a suitable climate, the Nordics are well positioned for large-scale AI infrastructure.”

In Australia, Win DC plans to deploy 11 MW of modular data centre capacity across renewable-energy sites, placing compute near wind, solar, and battery generation.

"Australia's energy transition depends on building AI infrastructure in the right place, where the renewable energy is, rather than waiting for a grid that can't scale fast enough to carry it," said Andrew Sjoquist, Founder and CEO of Win DC. "Leviathan lets us bring compute directly to clean power and scale it with the workload."

## Sixteen B200s, forty-eight Blackwells, free for SMEs — and a small request is answered in two to three working days: Cyprus opened its national AI machine to local companies

The useful fact in this story is not the hardware. It is that a Cypriot SME can get time on the national AI machine for nothing, applying any day of the year, with an answer inside a week. The Cyprus Information Technology Enterprises Association (CITEA), The Cyprus Institute and DiGiNN, the European Digital Innovation Hub of Cyprus, held an Open Day on the country's national High-Performance Computing and AI facility, Aphroditi, hosted at The Cyprus Institute for CITEA members. The programme covered infrastructure demonstrations, practical AI workflows, the process of getting access through DiGiNN, an introduction to European AI Factories and other EU resources, a roundtable on local industry needs, a facility tour and a Q&A.

On the date, the sources disagree and we are not going to pretend otherwise. Cyprus Mail's report, published 20 November, says the Open Day was held "today… Friday 20 November". reporter.com.cy and StockWatch, both publishing on 20 November, place it on Thursday 19 November. Both readings are internally consistent on the weekday, so one outlet is simply a day out. It was not 21 November — that is the date of the Cyprus Business Now digest that carried the item onward.

CITEA president George Malekkos is the only speaker named in the English coverage. "Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and advanced digital infrastructure has become an increasingly important factor in business competitiveness," he said, adding that "for Cypriot companies to fully benefit from these technologies, they need access not only to knowledge and expertise, but also to the appropriate infrastructure and tools." On the money: "Aphroditi represents an important national infrastructure, while the opportunity for SMEs to access its resources free of charge through DiGiNN creates new prospects for developing innovative solutions in Cyprus."

The access policy, which is the part worth reading properly. The facility operates two regimes. Relevance-driven access covers research, development and innovation by academia, research organisations, public bodies and SMEs — and in the operator's own words, "Access for these projects is provided free of charge." Market-driven access is charged at full cost, and it catches two groups: large companies doing R&D&I, under EU state-aid rules, and any purely commercial project regardless of company size. So the dividing line is not whether you are a business. It is how big you are and whether the work is research or production.

The turnaround times are published, which is unusual enough to be worth quoting. Allocations are measured in CPU and GPU hours, with a CPU ceiling of 200,000 hours per three-month period. A small-scale fast-track request — up to 3,000 B200 GPU-hours or 11,000 RTX GPU-hours — gets an internal decision in two to three working days. Medium-scale requests, 3,000–10,000 B200 hours or 11,000–25,000 RTX hours, go to a Project Review Committee within one week. Anything larger goes to a Project Advisory Committee case by case. Projects run in three-month cycles, renewable in three-month increments, and bigger appetites get pointed on to EuroHPC. Applications are accepted on a continuous, year-round basis — there is no call deadline to miss.

What is actually in the room. Per the operator's own resources page: a B200 cluster of two HGX B200 nodes, each with eight NVIDIA B200 at 192 GB of VRAM apiece, two Intel Xeon Platinum CPUs (64 cores) and 2,064 GB of high-bandwidth memory per node — sixteen B200s in total. Alongside it, an RTX6000 cluster of six nodes, each with eight NVIDIA RTX 6000 Blackwell at 96 GB, two AMD EPYC 9333 CPUs (64 cores) and 1,032 GB of RAM — forty-eight GPUs. Facility-wide there is HDR 100 InfiniBand and multi-petabyte shared storage. The older Cyclone system is being decommissioned. Aphroditi is described as part of the Cyprus Edge-AI Hub initiative, built on four stated principles: open access, free for R&D&I, data sovereignty, and pathways onward to European and EuroHPC resources. The funding reference is the EDGE-AI project OPEN INFRA/0625/0053, Research and Innovation Foundation with EU NextGenerationEU.

How you actually apply. Review the access conditions, create an account on the HPCF portal, submit a project application, and receive login details on approval. The old split between "Production" and "Preparatory" tracks has been replaced by that single process.

What nobody has published. There is no peak performance figure for Aphroditi on the operator's own pages — no petaflops number, no cooling detail, no in-service date. Any FLOPS figure circulating for this machine is not coming from the people who run it. Greek-language coverage of the Open Day adds two NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper units, 5 PB of local storage and a 400 Gb/s interconnect; none of those three appear on the facility's own specification page, so treat them as unconfirmed. The same goes for the figures circulating about Pharos-CY, the Cyprus AI Factory Antenna coordinated by The Cyprus Institute, and the share of the Greek DAEDALUS system reserved for Cyprus.

Why this sits on a competitions calendar. The BoC Fintech Hackathon 7.0 opens in Nicosia in six days and asks teams to reach Minimum Viable Product over a weekend, across thirteen tracks that lean heavily on AI. A fast-track allocation on sixteen B200s, answered in two to three working days and costing nothing, is the sort of thing that changes what a small team can credibly promise a jury — and almost nobody on the island appears to know it is there for the asking.
